title: Road Hazard and Battery Coverage Bought with the Crestline Credit Card: Returned-Fee Courtesy Addition
content:
Northgate's returned-fee courtesy credit on the Crestline Credit Card recognizes Crestline coverage bought with the card: a cardholder who holds an active Crestline road hazard certificate (Road Hazard Protection) paid with the Crestline card and an active Crestline battery warranty (Battery Replacement Warranties) paid with the Crestline card adds 0.1 to the share of the returned payment fee that the courtesy credit returns; one who holds exactly one of the two, active and paid with the card, adds 0.05; otherwise nothing is added. The share, with every addition made to it, never exceeds 1.0 — the whole fee.

| Road Hazard Protection certificate, active, paid with the Crestline card | Battery Replacement Warranties warranty, active, paid with the Crestline card | Added |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 0.1 (10 percentage points) |
| yes | no | 0.05 |
| no | yes | 0.05 |
| no | no | nothing |

**Records read.** For Road Hazard Protection, the cardholder's certificates — status active and the tender they were bought with; for Battery Replacement Warranties, the cardholder's battery warranties — status active and the tender used. Only the Crestline card as tender counts; coverage bought in cash, on another card or on a fleet account does not.

## Cases (hypothetical)

- An active battery warranty bought on the Crestline card and an expired road hazard certificate bought on the card: 0.05.
- Both active, both bought on the Crestline card: 0.1.
